newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end cautious session slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end cautious session slightly higher.

text.p: Stocks edged marginally higher on Monday, as investors struggled for a second straight session to assess recent evidence that the U.S. economy is outperforming expectations.

The Dow Jones industrial average rose 4.41 points to close at 8,198.45. Economically sensitive sectors such as retailing and technology led the advance, which snapped a brief, two-session losing streak for the blue-chip average.
In the broader market, advancing issues led decliners, 1,484 to 1,365, on moderate volume of 456 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index posted solid gains, rising 11.12 points to a record 1,605.45, helped by its weighting toward technology stocks.

Stocks rose despite weakness in the bond market, where interest rates continued to creep higher in the wake of strong manufacturing and employment figures released last Friday. The yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond climbed to 6.48 percent from 6.45 percent at Friday's close.
While concern about the pace of growth has bond investors on edge, the stock market has largely held its ground.

"For now, the strong economy is good news because it creates spending and that helps earnings," said Arnie Owen, managing director of capital markets at Cruttenden Roth. "We certainly aren't seeing any sign it's driving up prices."
What strength the Dow mustered came mostly from retail components Wal-Mart Stores Inc., up 1-3/16 to 37-7/8, and Sears, Roebuck & Co., up 2-1/8 to 64-3/8.

The higher close came a day ahead of a pair of weekly reports on the nation's retail sales activity. With Wall Street on alert for any sign of an overheating economy, the reports -- which often fluctuate erratically week to week -- will draw a high level of scrutiny.
"With the new case of jitters in the bond market, it certainly appears the retail numbers will get some attention," said Greg Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities.
"I still have a feeling we're underestimating just how strong the economy is, but even so, that is more of a hurdle for bonds than stocks," he said.

Technology stocks posted broad gains, with Dow components International Business Machines Corp. rising 1-1/2 to 106-1/4 and Hewlett-Packard Co. gaining 3/4 to 69-11/16. Intel Corp. led a sharp rally in computer chip stocks, climbing 3-1/8 points to 96-3/4.

Among individual issues, Alpha-Beta Technology Inc. skidded 4-11/16 to 6-1/8 after disappointing overall results in tests of the company's Betafectin drug for use in preventing post-surgical infections.
Perkins Family Restaurants LP climbed 2-1/8 to 13 after its 48-percent owner Restaurant Co. offered to buy the remaining 52 percent of the company for $13.00 per unit.
Nextel Communications Inc. jumped 2-13/16 to 26-11/16 after Morgan Stanley started coverage of the telecommunications company with a strong buy rating.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 3.16 points to 950.30.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues, also known as the Wilshire 5,000 -- rose 27.482, or 0.31 percent, to 9,005.064.
